blocks.source: Canto XXI
blocks.translation: Canto XXI

blocks.source: Così di ponte in ponte, altro parlando
blocks.translation: From bridge to bridge thus, speaking other things

blocks.source: che la mia comedìa cantar non cura,
blocks.translation: Of which my Comedy cares not to sing,

blocks.source: venimmo; e tenavamo ’l colmo, quando
blocks.translation: We came along, and held the summit, when

blocks.source: restammo per veder l’altra fessura
blocks.translation: We halted to behold another fissure

blocks.source: di Malebolge e li altri pianti vani;
blocks.translation: Of Malebolge and other vain laments;

blocks.source: e vidila mirabilmente oscura.
blocks.translation: And I beheld it marvellously dark.

blocks.source: Quale ne l’arzanà de’ Viniziani
blocks.translation: As in the Arsenal of the Venetians

blocks.source: bolle l’inverno la tenace pece
blocks.translation: Boils in the winter the tenacious pitch

blocks.source: a rimpalmare i legni lor non sani,
blocks.translation: To smear their unsound vessels o’er again,

blocks.source: ché navicar non ponno—in quella vece
blocks.translation: For sail they cannot; and instead thereof

blocks.source: chi fa suo legno novo e chi ristoppa
blocks.translation: One makes his vessel new, and one recaulks

blocks.source: le coste a quel che più vïaggi fece;
blocks.translation: The ribs of that which many a voyage has made;

blocks.source: chi ribatte da proda e chi da poppa;
blocks.translation: One hammers at the prow, one at the stern,

blocks.source: altri fa remi e altri volge sarte;
blocks.translation: This one makes oars, and that one cordage twists,

blocks.source: chi terzeruolo e artimon rintoppa—:
blocks.translation: Another mends the mainsail and the mizzen;

blocks.source: tal, non per foco ma per divin’ arte,
blocks.translation: Thus, not by fire, but by the art divine,

blocks.source: bollia là giuso una pegola spessa,
blocks.translation: Was boiling down below there a dense pitch

blocks.source: che ’nviscava la ripa d’ogne parte.
blocks.translation: Which upon every side the bank belimed.

blocks.source: I’ vedea lei, ma non vedëa in essa
blocks.translation: I saw it, but I did not see within it

blocks.source: mai che le bolle che ’l bollor levava,
blocks.translation: Aught but the bubbles that the boiling raised,

blocks.source: e gonfiar tutta, e riseder compressa.
blocks.translation: And all swell up and resubside compressed.

blocks.source: Mentr’ io là giù fisamente mirava,
blocks.translation: The while below there fixedly I gazed,

blocks.source: lo duca mio, dicendo «Guarda, guarda!»,
blocks.translation: My Leader, crying out: “Beware, beware!”

blocks.source: mi trasse a sé del loco dov’ io stava.
blocks.translation: Drew me unto himself from where I stood.

blocks.source: Allor mi volsi come l’uom cui tarda
blocks.translation: Then I turned round, as one who is impatient

blocks.source: di veder quel che li convien fuggire
blocks.translation: To see what it behoves him to escape,

blocks.source: e cui paura sùbita sgagliarda,
blocks.translation: And whom a sudden terror doth unman,

blocks.source: che, per veder, non indugia ’l partire:
blocks.translation: Who, while he looks, delays not his departure;

blocks.source: e vidi dietro a noi un diavol nero
blocks.translation: And I beheld behind us a black devil,

blocks.source: correndo su per lo scoglio venire.
blocks.translation: Running along upon the crag, approach.

blocks.source: Ahi quant’ elli era ne l’aspetto fero!
blocks.translation: Ah, how ferocious was he in his aspect!

blocks.source: e quanto mi parea ne l’atto acerbo,
blocks.translation: And how he seemed to me in action ruthless,

blocks.source: con l’ali aperte e sovra i piè leggero!
blocks.translation: With open wings and light upon his feet!

blocks.source: L’omero suo, ch’era aguto e superbo,
blocks.translation: His shoulders, which sharp-pointed were and high,

blocks.source: carcava un peccator con ambo l’anche,
blocks.translation: A sinner did encumber with both haunches,

blocks.source: e quei tenea de’ piè ghermito ’l nerbo.
blocks.translation: And he held clutched the sinews of the feet.

blocks.source: Del nostro ponte disse: «O Malebranche,
blocks.translation: From off our bridge, he said: “O Malebranche,

blocks.source: ecco un de li anzïan di Santa Zita!
blocks.translation: Behold one of the elders of Saint Zita;

blocks.source: Mettetel sotto, ch’i’ torno per anche
blocks.translation: Plunge him beneath, for I return for others

blocks.source: a quella terra, che n’è ben fornita:
blocks.translation: Unto that town, which is well furnished with them.

blocks.source: ogn’ uom v’è barattier, fuor che Bonturo;
blocks.translation: All there are barrators, except Bonturo;

blocks.source: del no, per li denar, vi si fa ita».
blocks.translation: No into Yes for money there is changed.”

blocks.source: Là giù ’l buttò, e per lo scoglio duro
blocks.translation: He hurled him down, and over the hard crag

blocks.source: si volse; e mai non fu mastino sciolto
blocks.translation: Turned round, and never was a mastiff loosened

blocks.source: con tanta fretta a seguitar lo furo.
blocks.translation: In so much hurry to pursue a thief.

blocks.source: Quel s’attuffò, e tornò sù convolto;
blocks.translation: The other sank, and rose again face downward;

blocks.source: ma i demon che del ponte avean coperchio,
blocks.translation: But the demons, under cover of the bridge,

blocks.source: gridar: «Qui non ha loco il Santo Volto!
blocks.translation: Cried: “Here the Santo Volto has no place!

blocks.source: qui si nuota altrimenti che nel Serchio!
blocks.translation: Here swims one otherwise than in the Serchio;

blocks.source: Però, se tu non vuo’ di nostri graffi,
blocks.translation: Therefore, if for our gaffs thou wishest not,

blocks.source: non far sopra la pegola soverchio».
blocks.translation: Do not uplift thyself above the pitch.”

blocks.source: Poi l’addentar con più di cento raffi,
blocks.translation: They seized him then with more than a hundred rakes;

blocks.source: disser: «Coverto convien che qui balli,
blocks.translation: They said: “It here behoves thee to dance covered,

blocks.source: sì che, se puoi, nascosamente accaffi».
blocks.translation: That, if thou canst, thou secretly mayest pilfer.”

blocks.source: Non altrimenti i cuoci a’ lor vassalli
blocks.translation: Not otherwise the cooks their scullions make

blocks.source: fanno attuffare in mezzo la caldaia
blocks.translation: Immerse into the middle of the caldron

blocks.source: la carne con li uncin, perché non galli.
blocks.translation: The meat with hooks, so that it may not float.

blocks.source: Lo buon maestro «Acciò che non si paia
blocks.translation: Said the good Master to me: “That it be not

blocks.source: che tu ci sia», mi disse, «giù t’acquatta
blocks.translation: Apparent thou art here, crouch thyself down

blocks.source: dopo uno scheggio, ch’alcun schermo t’aia;
blocks.translation: Behind a jag, that thou mayest have some screen;

blocks.source: e per nulla offension che mi sia fatta,
blocks.translation: And for no outrage that is done to me

blocks.source: non temer tu, ch’i’ ho le cose conte,
blocks.translation: Be thou afraid, because these things I know,

blocks.source: perch’ altra volta fui a tal baratta».
blocks.translation: For once before was I in such a scuffle.”

blocks.source: Poscia passò di là dal co del ponte;
blocks.translation: Then he passed on beyond the bridge’s head,

blocks.source: e com’ el giunse in su la ripa sesta,
blocks.translation: And as upon the sixth bank he arrived,

blocks.source: mestier li fu d’aver sicura fronte.
blocks.translation: Need was for him to have a steadfast front.

blocks.source: Con quel furore e con quella tempesta
blocks.translation: With the same fury, and the same uproar,

blocks.source: ch’escono i cani a dosso al poverello
blocks.translation: As dogs leap out upon a mendicant,

blocks.source: che di sùbito chiede ove s’arresta,
blocks.translation: Who on a sudden begs, where’er he stops,

blocks.source: usciron quei di sotto al ponticello,
blocks.translation: They issued from beneath the little bridge,

blocks.source: e volser contra lui tutt’ i runcigli;
blocks.translation: And turned against him all their grappling-irons;

blocks.source: ma el gridò: «Nessun di voi sia fello!
blocks.translation: But he cried out: “Be none of you malignant!

blocks.source: Innanzi che l’uncin vostro mi pigli,
blocks.translation: Before those hooks of yours lay hold of me,

blocks.source: traggasi avante l’un di voi che m’oda,
blocks.translation: Let one of you step forward, who may hear me,

blocks.source: e poi d’arruncigliarmi si consigli».
blocks.translation: And then take counsel as to grappling me.”

blocks.source: Tutti gridaron: «Vada Malacoda!»;
blocks.translation: They all cried out: “Let Malacoda go;”

blocks.source: per ch’un si mosse—e li altri stetter fermi—
blocks.translation: Whereat one started, and the rest stood still,

blocks.source: e venne a lui dicendo: «Che li approda?».
blocks.translation: And he came to him, saying: “What avails it?”

blocks.source: «Credi tu, Malacoda, qui vedermi
blocks.translation: “Thinkest thou, Malacoda, to behold me

blocks.source: esser venuto», disse ’l mio maestro,
blocks.translation: Advanced into this place,” my Master said,

blocks.source: «sicuro già da tutti vostri schermi,
blocks.translation: “Safe hitherto from all your skill of fence,

blocks.source: sanza voler divino e fato destro?
blocks.translation: Without the will divine, and fate auspicious?

blocks.source: Lascian’ andar, ché nel cielo è voluto
blocks.translation: Let me go on, for it in Heaven is willed

blocks.source: ch’i’ mostri altrui questo cammin silvestro».
blocks.translation: That I another show this savage road.”

blocks.source: Allor li fu l’orgoglio sì caduto,
blocks.translation: Then was his arrogance so humbled in him,

blocks.source: ch’e’ si lasciò cascar l’uncino a’ piedi,
blocks.translation: That he let fall his grapnel at his feet,

blocks.source: e disse a li altri: «Omai non sia feruto».
blocks.translation: And to the others said: “Now strike him not.”

blocks.source: E ’l duca mio a me: «O tu che siedi
blocks.translation: And unto me my Guide: “O thou, who sittest

blocks.source: tra li scheggion del ponte quatto quatto,
blocks.translation: Among the splinters of the bridge crouched down,

blocks.source: sicuramente omai a me ti riedi».
blocks.translation: Securely now return to me again.”

blocks.source: Per ch’io mi mossi e a lui venni ratto;
blocks.translation: Wherefore I started and came swiftly to him;

blocks.source: e i diavoli si fecer tutti avanti,
blocks.translation: And all the devils forward thrust themselves,

blocks.source: sì ch’io temetti ch’ei tenesser patto;
blocks.translation: So that I feared they would not keep their compact.

blocks.source: così vid’ ïo già temer li fanti
blocks.translation: And thus beheld I once afraid the soldiers

blocks.source: ch’uscivan patteggiati di Caprona,
blocks.translation: Who issued under safeguard from Caprona,

blocks.source: veggendo sé tra nemici cotanti.
blocks.translation: Seeing themselves among so many foes.

blocks.source: I’ m’accostai con tutta la persona
blocks.translation: Close did I press myself with all my person

blocks.source: lungo ’l mio duca, e non torceva li occhi
blocks.translation: Beside my Leader, and turned not mine eyes

blocks.source: da la sembianza lor ch’era non buona.
blocks.translation: From off their countenance, which was not good.

blocks.source: Ei chinavan li raffi e «Vuo’ che ’l tocchi»,
blocks.translation: They lowered their rakes, and “Wilt thou have me hit him,”

blocks.source: diceva l’un con l’altro, «in sul groppone?».
blocks.translation: They said to one another, “on the rump?”

blocks.source: E rispondien: «Sì, fa che gliel’ accocchi».
blocks.translation: And answered: “Yes; see that thou nick him with it.”

blocks.source: Ma quel demonio che tenea sermone
blocks.translation: But the same demon who was holding parley

blocks.source: col duca mio, si volse tutto presto
blocks.translation: With my Conductor turned him very quickly,

blocks.source: e disse: «Posa, posa, Scarmiglione!».
blocks.translation: And said: “Be quiet, be quiet, Scarmiglione;”

blocks.source: Poi disse a noi: «Più oltre andar per questo
blocks.translation: Then said to us: “You can no farther go

blocks.source: iscoglio non si può, però che giace
blocks.translation: Forward upon this crag, because is lying

blocks.source: tutto spezzato al fondo l’arco sesto.
blocks.translation: All shattered, at the bottom, the sixth arch.

blocks.source: E se l’andare avante pur vi piace,
blocks.translation: And if it still doth please you to go onward,

blocks.source: andatevene su per questa grotta;
blocks.translation: Pursue your way along upon this rock;

blocks.source: presso è un altro scoglio che via face.
blocks.translation: Near is another crag that yields a path.

blocks.source: Ier, più oltre cinqu’ ore che quest’ otta,
blocks.translation: Yesterday, five hours later than this hour,

blocks.source: mille dugento con sessanta sei
blocks.translation: One thousand and two hundred sixty-six

blocks.source: anni compié che qui la via fu rotta.
blocks.translation: Years were complete, that here the way was broken.

blocks.source: Io mando verso là di questi miei
blocks.translation: I send in that direction some of mine

blocks.source: a riguardar s’alcun se ne sciorina;
blocks.translation: To see if any one doth air himself;

blocks.source: gite con lor, che non saranno rei».
blocks.translation: Go ye with them; for they will not be vicious.

blocks.source: «Tra’ti avante, Alichino, e Calcabrina»,
blocks.translation: Step forward, Alichino and Calcabrina,”

blocks.source: cominciò elli a dire, «e tu, Cagnazzo;
blocks.translation: Began he to cry out, “and thou, Cagnazzo;

blocks.source: e Barbariccia guidi la decina.
blocks.translation: And Barbariccia, do thou guide the ten.

blocks.source: Libicocco vegn’ oltre e Draghignazzo,
blocks.translation: Come forward, Libicocco and Draghignazzo,

blocks.source: Cirïatto sannuto e Graffiacane
blocks.translation: And tusked Ciriatto and Graffiacane,

blocks.source: e Farfarello e Rubicante pazzo.
blocks.translation: And Farfarello and mad Rubicante;

blocks.source: Cercate ’ntorno le boglienti pane;
blocks.translation: Search ye all round about the boiling pitch;

blocks.source: costor sian salvi infino a l’altro scheggio
blocks.translation: Let these be safe as far as the next crag,

blocks.source: che tutto intero va sovra le tane».
blocks.translation: That all unbroken passes o’er the dens.”

blocks.source: «Omè, maestro, che è quel ch’i’ veggio?»,
blocks.translation: “O me! what is it, Master, that I see?

blocks.source: diss’ io, «deh, sanza scorta andianci soli,
blocks.translation: Pray let us go,” I said, “without an escort,

blocks.source: se tu sa’ ir; ch’i’ per me non la cheggio.
blocks.translation: If thou knowest how, since for myself I ask none.

blocks.source: Se tu se’ sì accorto come suoli,
blocks.translation: If thou art as observant as thy wont is,

blocks.source: non vedi tu ch’e’ digrignan li denti
blocks.translation: Dost thou not see that they do gnash their teeth,

blocks.source: e con le ciglia ne minaccian duoli?».
blocks.translation: And with their brows are threatening woe to us?”

blocks.source: Ed elli a me: «Non vo’ che tu paventi;
blocks.translation: And he to me: “I will not have thee fear;

blocks.source: lasciali digrignar pur a lor senno,
blocks.translation: Let them gnash on, according to their fancy,

blocks.source: ch’e’ fanno ciò per li lessi dolenti».
blocks.translation: Because they do it for those boiling wretches.”

blocks.source: Per l’argine sinistro volta dienno;
blocks.translation: Along the left-hand dike they wheeled about;

blocks.source: ma prima avea ciascun la lingua stretta
blocks.translation: But first had each one thrust his tongue between

blocks.source: coi denti, verso lor duca, per cenno;
blocks.translation: His teeth towards their leader for a signal;

blocks.source: ed elli avea del cul fatto trombetta.
blocks.translation: And he had made a trumpet of his rump.
